question: The Joint Sitting of the parliament is governed by the rules of ___________

options.text: Special Rules mentioned by the Cabinet

solution:
The correct answer is __**1. Lok Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 108** of the Indian Constitution provides for a Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) to resolve disagreements on legislative matters.
 
• The **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** presides over the Joint Sitting, as explicitly mentioned in the Constitution. This is irrespective of whether the bill originated in the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha.
 
• In the Speaker’s absence, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides. If both are unavailable, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha may preside. *Hence, Option 1 is correct.*
 
• The rules of procedure of the Lok Sabha govern the conduct of the Joint Sitting. These rules ensure smooth functioning and decision-making during such sessions.
 
• The Joint Sitting provision is used sparingly and is considered a mechanism to address legislative deadlocks in the Indian parliamentary system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 108 of the Constitution:**

 
 
• This article empowers the President of India to summon a Joint Sitting of Parliament to resolve disagreements between the two Houses on a bill.
 
• A Joint Sitting is convened when one House passes a bill, and the other House either rejects it, proposes amendments not agreeable to the originating House, or fails to take any action within six months.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lok Sabha and Speaker:**
 
 
• As the Lok Sabha represents the majority of elected representatives, its Speaker presides over the Joint Sitting to ensure democratic representation in decision-making.
 
• The Speaker’s role is crucial in maintaining order and ensuring the rules of the Lok Sabha are followed during the Joint Sitting.
 
 
 
• **Historical Instances of Joint Sitting:**
 
 
• The first Joint Sitting was held in 1961 to pass the Dowry Prohibition Bill, 1959, which had faced disagreements between the two Houses.
 
• Another notable Joint Sitting was held in 2002 to pass the Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA), which had been a contentious issue between the Houses.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Joint Sitting:**
 
 
• It is a unique provision in India’s bicameral legislature, designed to prevent legislative paralysis.
 
• The decision in a Joint Sitting is taken by a majority vote of the members present and voting, ensuring equal participation of both Houses.
